The culprit is the `target` directory (4.25 GB) in the sentinel parent directory. That's the Rust build cache from Cargo—it contains compiled artifacts, dependencies, and intermediate build files. This is completely normal for a Rust project.

If you want to reclaim that space:

```powershell
# Clean cargo build artifacts (safe to run anytime)
cargo clean
```

This will delete the entire `target` directory and free up ~4 GB. You can rebuild anytime with `cargo build` or `cargo test`. Alternatively, if you want to keep binaries but delete expensive intermediate artifacts:

```powershell
# Just clean the debug builds (keeps release if you built those)
rm -r target/debug
```

The git repository itself (`.git` folder) is actually tiny and fine—it's just that Rust projects accumulate large build caches over time.
